description:
EDIT A CLOUD FOR WORDPRESS SITE'S CONTENT: pages, posts, menus, categories, comments, site title and anything else in the WordPress REST API. This is the tool to use when the user asks to change what is on their WordPress site. It runs one REST call inside the site, so no password or extra setup is needed. `path` is the REST route without /wp-json, e.g.:
- list pages: GET /wp/v2/pages with query {"_fields": "id,title,link,status"}
- read a page to edit it: GET /wp/v2/pages/12 with query {"context": "edit"} (content.raw is the block markup to change)
- update it: POST /wp/v2/pages/12 with body {"content": "..."} (send the whole new content, keeping the <!-- wp:... --> block comments)
- new post: POST /wp/v2/posts with body {"title": "...", "content": "...", "status": "draft"} (draft first, publish when the user says so)
- menus: /wp/v2/navigation, /wp/v2/menu-items; search: GET /wp/v2/search?search=...
It acts as the `porkbun-agent` WordPress editor by default (pages, posts, media, comments). Site settings (title, tagline, homepage), plugins, themes and users need `as_administrator: true` with `acknowledge_full_access: true`; ask the user first. Use _fields and per_page to keep answers small. Show the user what will change before overwriting a page, and offer create_wordpress_backup before big edits. Images: upload with wordpress_upload_media, then use its id or url. WordPress's own errors come back as WP_REST_ERROR with httpStatus and its message.

acknowledge_full_access.description: Confirms the user agreed to administrator-level changes.

as_administrator.description: Act as the site administrator (settings, plugins, themes, users). Needs acknowledge_full_access.

domain.description: The domain of the Cloud for WordPress site, e.g. `example.com`.

dry_run.description: For writes: check the request without sending it to WordPress.

embed.description: Include linked resources (_embed), e.g. the featured image.

method.description: HTTP method (default GET). POST updates an existing item when the path has its id.

path.description: REST route, e.g. `/wp/v2/pages` or `/wp/v2/posts/42`. No query string: use `query`.
